The evidence pack of the month's closed statement: its sealed leaf, the signed daily checkpoint that covers it and an inclusion proof. Verify it offline with `sentech_verify.py` together with the statement file and Sentech's published keys. 409 `statement_seal_pending` until a daily checkpoint covers the statement.

The month's statement lines as CSV (UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, CRLF lines): ids, SAST time, kind and integer cents with a running held-funds balance, then per-kind totals and the opening/closing balance. Streamed in keyset pages from one snapshot; audited before the first byte. Refused with 422 beyond 500,000 lines.

Whether the month's statement is closed and sealed in the Sentech record log. status is one of open | closed_unsealed | sealed_pending_checkpoint | sealed; seal_id appears once a signed daily checkpoint covers it. 404 when the period has no lines and no closed statement.

post.description: The body is limited to `coverage_import_max_bytes` (10 MB at most, the edge limit): a larger body is 413 `payload_too_large` and is refused while it streams. The whole body must arrive within `coverage_import_read_timeout_seconds` (60 s by default, about 170 kB/s for 10 MB), else 408 `request_timeout`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. 409 `import_in_progress`, 429 `import_capacity` and 503 `dataset_busy` are retryable and carry `Retry-After`.

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. Limited to 10 per admin per hour and 50 per tenant per day.

Send a login code. The answer is the same 202 whether or not the phone has an account.

Send a fresh `binding` secret (see the field) and keep it for `otp/verify`: a code can only

within the replay window.

post.description: Redeems a voucher code for the signed-in customer. Every code that cannot be redeemed answers the same 422 `voucher_invalid`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header; the body is limited to 2048 bytes.
Idempotent by construction: repeated calls return the order's one open attempt.

Server-to-server postback on the ONE central notify URL (Sentech's Netcash account has a
single URL for every ISP). The HMAC token in the URL proves only that the gateway sent it;
the ISP is then found from the identifiers the gateway echoes, never from the URL.

Never log `token` or the request path: the URL is the credential (the access log masks it).

get.description:
Work waiting across the Sentech queues, as one list: refunds, review cases, bank
exceptions, payout batches and exceptions, onboarding decisions and steps, erasures, clawbacks,
router approvals and the integrity pause. `can_act` is false when the caller asked for the
item themselves (four eyes) or holds the read-only finance role (then open items wait on
others). At most 50 per kind; `truncated` says so.

The audit trail across tenants, newest first. Reading it is itself audited (filters and
count, never rows) under the Sentech tenant.

put.description:
Assign a tier with optional limit overrides (null = unlimited). A priced tier also sets
the ISP's monthly subscription amount, keeping its billing day and active flag.

`keep_overrides: true` changes the tier only and keeps the tenant's current overrides as they
are when the change commits (do not send `overrides` with it); without it the overrides are
replaced by `overrides` (default none), exactly as before.

post.description:
Ask for an offboarded tenant's data to be purged (first of two platform admins). Refused
(409 `purge_not_eligible`, with `blockers`) unless the tenant has been offboarded for the
retention window, is not the platform owner, has no legal hold, no payment awaiting review
and no usable voucher export link. One open request per tenant.

schema.description:

reference) stay on the request and never reach the audit log: no personal data in them.
schema.title: PurgeRequestIn

The request; once completed, the certificate of erasure (counts, verification,
approvers, checklist).

post.description:
Second platform admin. Starts the cooling-off period (either admin may cancel in it);
eligibility is checked again. A repeated approval is a no-op.

Cancel a requested, approved (cooling-off) or failed request. Any platform admin may stop
a purge; a running one finishes its current batch first and cannot be cancelled. Needs a
recent sign-in like the other purge steps (review LOW-3).

Confirm one out-of-database step (object store prefix, Redis keys, Keycloak users,
FreeRADIUS clients re-render, backup window) as done; recorded with the actor and time.

Send a failed request back. A failure on eligibility, or before any row was deleted, returns
it to `requested`: a new approval by an admin other than the requester and the retrier, and a
fresh cooling-off. Only a technical failure after deletion started resumes as `approved`; each
batch re-checks eligibility and continues where the last committed batch stopped.

default. The OTP limiter reads it within 30 seconds on every worker (at once on the one that
handled this call). Naturally idempotent; a change is audited with before and after.

Proposes reopening an ISP staff member's authenticator-enrolment window for 24 hours.

request.

put.description:
Replace the tenant's published support email and phone (shown on its website and in

post.description:
Suspend a trial or active tenant: its customers and staff are refused from then on
(403 `tenant_suspended` / 404 `tenant_not_found`); payment notifications are still recorded
but grant nothing. Repeating it is a no-op.

Optional body `{confirm_slug, reason}` (the console always sends both): a `confirm_slug` that
is not the tenant's slug is refused (422 `slug_mismatch`), `reason` (contract_ended,
non_payment, tenant_request, abuse, other) is recorded in the audit. An Idempotency-Key is
honoured when sent.

schema.description:
Optional body of suspend. The console always sends both fields; when `confirm_slug` is
present it must equal the tenant's slug.

get.description: The evidence pack of the statement a verify token names, for the person the ISP gave the link to (the verify page reads the token from the URL fragment). post.description: Send a message to the tenant's support team. Requires a Turnstile token and an Idempotency-Key header. The message is stored encrypted and emailed to the tenant's support address; the answer is a reference to quote. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key and body returns the stored answer without a new Turnstile check. The body is limited to 16384 bytes.
